title: Business license (BPOL), business tangible property or machinery and tools tax, and the County tax registrations for a glass studio
question: Once my glass studio has zoning approval in Albemarle County, how do I get the County business license, how is a studio that makes, sells and teaches classified and taxed, how do I report the furnaces, kilns and tools, and what other County tax registrations (food and beverage, ABC flat fees) apply?
office: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit); the Director of Finance holds the commissioner of the revenue's assessing powers because the County has no elected Commissioner of the Revenue
summary: Albemarle County has no Commissioner of the Revenue: the Department of Finance & Budget's Office of Revenue Administration licenses businesses and assesses business property. After zoning approval, send the New Business License Application by email or mail (no online account opening for a new business) with your SSN or federal ID, any SCC trade name or entity registration, and a contractor license if you contract. There is no fee under $25,000 of gross receipts (file anyway), a $50 fee from $25,000 to under $100,000, and at $100,000 and above a tax by classification: retail sales $0.20 per $100 of gross receipts, repair, personal, business and other services (which is where classes and custom work usually fall) $0.36 per $100; a manufacturer selling at wholesale at the place of manufacture is exempt from BPOL by state law, so how the County classifies the studio matters. Renew every year by March 1, with rate-based tax due June 15. Report furnaces, glory holes, kilns, tools, furniture and fixtures on the Business Tangible Personal Property return by May 1 each year ($4.28 per $100 of assessed value, assessed at 25% of cost in year one down to 10% from year seven; billed in two halves); if the County classifies the studio as a manufacturer, production equipment is reported separately as machinery and tools at the same rate. A cafe registers for the 6% food and beverage tax and an ABC licensee pays the County's alcohol flat fee. A sign permit comes from Community Development, not Finance.

steps.step: Get zoning approval first, and decide how many licenses you need
steps.who: You; Community Development (zoning); Office of Revenue Administration
steps.how: The County's Start a Business page sends you to Community Development for zoning approval (a Zoning Clearance, or a Home Occupation Clearance for a studio at home; see glass_studio_zoning_use) before the license. A license is required for each business and each definite place of business; a studio that makes glass, sells it and teaches classes at one address may elect one license for all its activities carried on at that place, or the County may license and classify the activities separately. Under $25,000 of gross receipts the County waives the license requirement but still asks you to file.
steps.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(1); Albemarle County Code § 8-200; Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Start a Business page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026)
steps.paraphrase: The County lists things to have ready before you send in the New Business License Application.

steps.step: Gather the prerequisites: tax ID, SCC registrations, contractor license
steps.how: Have your Social Security Number or federal employer ID ready a copy of the trade-name (assumed-name) certificate filed with the SCC if you use a trade name; a copy of your SCC registration if the studio is an LLC, corporation, partnership or business trust; and a copy of your contractor's license from the State Board of Contractors if you contract. Fill in the New Business License Application (PDF) from the County's Finance pages.
steps.basis: Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Start a Business page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026)
steps.paraphrase: Bring a copy of your SCC trade name registration if the business trades under a name.

steps.step: Send the application to the Office of Revenue Administration by email or mail
steps.who: You; Office of Revenue Administration, Business & Personal Tax Unit
steps.how: Email the completed application and copies to tax@albemarle.org or mail them to County of Albemarle, 401 McIntire Rd, Room 133, Charlottesville, VA 22902 (the County's business tax portal is for renewals and payments, not for opening a new account). State law and the County Code say to apply before beginning business; the County's forms allow 30 days from the start date (see bpol_business_license). Pay the $50 fee with the application if your expected gross receipts are $25,000 to under $100,000; if $100,000 or more, a new business pays tax on its estimate when it applies.
steps.deadline: Before beginning business (the County form allows 30 days from the start date)
steps.fee: No fee under $25,000; $50 from $25,000 to under $100,000; rate-based tax at $100,000 and above
steps.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(a); Albemarle County Code § 8-201(A); Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Start a Business page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026)
steps.paraphrase: With the prerequisites in hand, you send the application to Revenue Administration by mail or email.

steps.step: Understand how the studio is classified, and ask for a written ruling if it matters
steps.who: You; the Director of Finance (Office of Revenue Administration)
steps.how: The County's rate table taxes retailers at $0.20 per $100 of gross receipts (gallery sales of your own and consigned work); repair, personal, business and other services at $0.36 per $100 (classes, workshops, commissions and studio rental usually fall here); and wholesalers at $0.05 per $100 of purchases. State law bars a BPOL tax on a manufacturer for manufacturing and selling at wholesale at the place of manufacture, so a studio that mostly wholesales its own production may be exempt on those receipts while still licensed for retail and classes; the manufacturer label also moves your equipment into the machinery and tools class (step s6). Because the classification changes both taxes, you may ask the Director of Finance for a written ruling on your situation.
steps.basis: Va. Code §§ 58.1-3703(C)(4), 58.1-3703.1(A)(8), 58.1-3706(A); Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Tax Rates page (Internet Archive copy of 17 April 2026)
steps.paraphrase: The County's rate table has a line for repair, personal, business and other services.
steps.quote: Repair, Personal, Business and Other Services

steps.step: Renew every year by March 1 and pay rate-based tax by June 15
steps.how: Every license is renewed by March 1 using the prior year's gross receipts, online through the County's business tax portal (albemarlecountytaxes.org) or on paper; for the first three years a new business renews on the full application. If gross receipts were $100,000 or more the tax is billed and due June 15. Late filing or payment carries a 10% penalty plus interest; an extension can be requested before the due date for reasonable cause. The bpol_business_license file has the full renewal, extension, penalty and closing steps.
steps.deadline: Renewal by March 1; rate-based tax by June 15
steps.fee: $50 fee tier, or the rate-based tax; 10% late penalty
steps.quote: If the tax is measured by the gross receipts of the business, the tax shall be paid on or before June 15 of the license year

steps.step: File the Business Tangible Personal Property return (and machinery and tools, if classified as a manufacturer) by May 1
steps.how: Every business files a BTPP return by May 1 each year listing all tangible property on hand on January 1, by year of acquisition and at full original cost including sales tax, freight and installation (furniture, fixtures, computers, tools, shop equipment, machinery, and the furnace, glory hole, kilns, annealers, benches and torches). Attach an itemized list; small items under $500 may be grouped as an aggregate estimate, and equipment under $25 that is not machinery and tools need not be reported. Report leased equipment by lessor name and address, not cost. File online at albemarlecountytaxes.org or on the paper return, or send the itemized list by email or mail. Businesses classified as manufacturers (also miners, dairies, broadcasters, dry cleaners) report machinery and tools separately; processors report both machinery and tools and furniture, fixtures and equipment. If the business owns no property it must still file saying so. The tax is $4.28 per $100 of assessed value, assessed at 25% of original cost in the first year, 22.5% in the second, 20%, 17.5%, 15%, 12.5%, and 10% from the seventh year; it is not prorated if the business closes mid-year.
steps.deadline: May 1 each year; the County page gives June 25 and December 5 as the 2025 half-year due dates
steps.fee: $4.28 per $100 of assessed value (BTPP and machinery and tools)
steps.basis: Va. Code §§ 58.1-3507, 58.1-3518; Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Business Tangible Personal Property & Machinery and Tools page (Internet Archive copy of 12 June 2026)
steps.paraphrase: The business tangible property return is due every May 1.

steps.step: If you serve food or drink: register for the food and beverage tax and the County's ABC flat-fee license
steps.who: You; Office of Revenue Administration, Business & Personal Tax Unit
steps.how: Any business that prepares and serves food or drink collects the County's 6% food and beverage tax and remits it by the 20th of each month (online or on the printable return); register with the Business & Personal Tax Unit when you get the business license. The County's rate table also lists alcoholic beverage flat fees by ABC license class (beer on premises $25; beer and wine on premises $37.50; mixed beverages up to 100 seats $200, 101 to 150 seats $350, 151 or more $500), paid alongside the state ABC license. See glass_studio_food_and_events for the Health District and ABC steps.
steps.deadline: Food and beverage tax returns by the 20th of each month
steps.fee: Food and beverage tax 6%; ABC flat fees by class (see fees)
steps.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3833; Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Food & Beverage Tax page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026) and Tax Rates page (Internet Archive copy of 17 April 2026)
steps.paraphrase: A business collecting food and beverage tax must register with the Business & Personal Tax Unit, hold a business license, and file and pay the return every month.

steps.step: Sales tax, utility taxes and signs: know which are not Finance's
steps.who: You; Virginia Department of Taxation; Community Development (signs)
steps.how: The 1% local option retail sales tax (5.3% combined) on glass sales and class materials is registered and paid through the Virginia Department of Taxation, not the County. Consumer utility taxes on commercial gas and electricity (for example $0.0638 per CCF of gas for the first 4,500 CCF on non-interruptible commercial service) are collected by the utilities on your bills. A sign permit comes from Community Development after the Zoning Clearance (see glass_studio_zoning_use), not from Finance.
steps.fee: Retail sales and use tax 5.3% (4.3% state plus 1% local); consumer utility taxes per the County's rate table
steps.basis: Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Other Consumer Taxes page (Internet Archive copy of 12 June 2026) and Tax Rates page (Internet Archive copy of 17 April 2026)
steps.paraphrase: The County's 1% local sales tax rides on the state sales tax and is handled by the Virginia Department of Taxation.

steps.step: If you disagree with a classification or assessment: appeal in writing
steps.who: You; Director of Finance; Virginia Tax Commissioner
steps.how: File a written administrative appeal with the Director of Finance within one year of the assessment or appealable event; the Director's determination can be appealed to the Virginia Tax Commissioner within 90 days, and then to circuit court. Collection of the disputed amount is generally suspended while the appeal is pending. The bpol_business_license file gives the full route and the County's appeal page.
steps.deadline: Local appeal within one year; Tax Commissioner within 90 days of the local determination
steps.quote: Any person assessed with a local license tax as a result of an appealable event as defined in this section may file an administrative appeal of the assessment within one year from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of the appealable event, whichever is later, with the commissioner of the revenue or other local assessing official.

caveats: www.albemarle.org refuses automated readers; the Finance pages cited are Internet Archive copies (dates in the sources) and County quotes carry paraphrases because the County's terms bar reposting. County Code Chapter 8 quotes come from the 2019 ordinance text on the County's Legistar API, as in bpol_business_license.

Whether a glass studio is a 'manufacturer' for BPOL (wholesale sales at the place of manufacture exempt) and for machinery and tools tax is a classification the Director of Finance makes; nothing on the County's pages addresses artisan or craft production. Ask for a written ruling if the amounts matter.
The BTPP page's half-year due dates (June 25 and December 5) are stated for 2025; check the current year's dates on the County's deadlines page.
The itemized-list email address on the BTPP page ends in albemarle.com rather than albemarle.org; it is recorded as published and should be confirmed.
The New Business License Application, BTPP return and food and beverage tax form PDFs were not read.
